*281. SHRI GIREESH KUMAR
SANGHI:
DR. T. SUBBARAMI
REDDY:
Will the Minister of FINANCE be
pleased to state:
(a) whether World Bank has signalled
its intention to open up new opportunity
for engagement with India's largest and
poorest States;
(b) if so, whether World Bank has
changed its strategy for lending to States;
(c) whether World Ba n k group
strategy has decided to retain an essential
reform and performance based approach
to States;
(d) if so, to what extent this new strategy
of World Bank has affected India for lending;
and
(e) to what extent India has been able to
follow changes that have been made by
World Bank for lending?

*282. SHRI DIPANKAR
MUKHERJEE:
SHRI CHITTABRATA
MAJUMDAR:
Will the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION
be pleased to state:
(a) whether Airports Authority of India
(AAI) had gone to the Delhi High Court
for obtaining a stay order on the Labour
Ministry's Notification No. S.O./848(E)
dated the 26th July, 2004 prohibiting
employment of contract labour in the job
of trolley retrieval;
(b) whether AAI had approached the
High Power Committee established by
Government pursuant to Supreme Court
order dated the 11th September, 1991
before going to Court; and
(c) if not, the reasons therefor and the
action taken against those responsible for
by-passing High Power Committee?

PROF. ALKA BALRAM
KSHATRIYA:
Will the Minister of FINANCE be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Reserve Bank of India (RBI)
is monitoring and supervising the role of
Nationalised Banks and Financial
Institutions (FIs) through any advisory
group;
(b) if so, what are the names of Banks/
FIs which are under active scanner of the
RBI; and
(c) whether any irregularities have been
found in the working of these Banks/FIs
and if so, the details thereof?

state:

to approve the public offer plan mooted

to Government every year; and

Petitions against Air India
Management
1900. SHRI SANJAY  RAUT: Will the
Minister of CIVIL AVIATION be pleased
to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that 419 writ
petitions are pending in several courts in
India filed by Air India employees against
the Air India Management;
(b) if so, whether it conveys collapse
of administrative machinery, high-
handedness, lack of transparency in the
decision making process and arbitrary use
of power and authority by Air India
officials; and
(c) the measures taken by the Air India
Management to curb abusive use of power
and authority by high officials, to ensure
that employee discontent and grievance is
redressed and misuse of power with
malafide intentions curbed, and to ensure
employee satisfaction and improved
productivity?
Entry of private airlines in
international sector
1901. SHRIMATI SAVITA SHARDA:
SHRI K. CHANDRAN PILLAI:
SHRI A. VIJAYARAGHAVAN:
SHRI ANAND SHARMA:
Will the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION
be pleased to state:
(a) whether private airlines were
allowed to expand their international
operations to more destinations including
services to South Asian Association for
Regional Co-operation (SAARC);
(b) if so, the details including private
airlines and destinations allowed as on
today;
(c) whether steps will be taken to allow
national carriers (Indian Airlines and Air
India) to induct capacity by expanding their
fleet renewal programmes to meet long
term capacity needs on international routes;
(d) if so, the details thereof; and
(e) whether competent authority will
postpone the sanction given to private airlines
till national carriers strengthen their fleet?

Landing rights for foreign airlines
1902. SHRIMATI PREMA
CARIAPPA:
SHRI ANAND SHARMA:
PROF. ALKA BALRAM
KSHATRIYA:
Will the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION
be pleased to state:
(a) the number of foreign airlines which
have been given landing rights by India in
cities other than International gateways;
(b) the names of the foreign airlines and
the indian cities for which such rights have
been granted;
(c) whether the foreign countries
concerned have given reciprocal rights to
Indian Carriers; and
(d) the details for five year period from
1999-2004 country and airline-wise?
Entry of private airlines in
international sector
1903. SHRI SK. KHABIR UDDIN
AHMED:
SHRI GIREESH KUMAR
SANGHI:
Will the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION
be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Government
have cleared the proposal of allowing
private airlines to fly foreign skies;
(b) if so, the rationale behind such a
move; and
(c) whether it will affect the income/
business of State Carriers?
Discounted fares on Goa-London
sector
1904. SHRI RAJU PARMAR: Will the
Minister of CIVIL AVIATION be pleased
to state:
(a) whether Government are aware that
a large number of private international
carriers are flying to Goa from London and
other European countries during this
season;
(b) whether Government are also aware
that these private airlines are offering Goa-
London return fare at about Rs. 16,000/-
per passenger; and
(c) if so, what steps Government
propose to take to match this fare on Air
India's flight to London and Europe?
Commercial use of Safdarjung Airport
1905. SHRI RAVULA CHANDRA
SEKAR REDDY: Will the Minister of
CIVIL AVIATION be pleased to state:
(a) whether there is a proposal to use
Safdarjung Airport for commercial
activities;
(b) if so, whether it would tamper with
the heritage status of the area;
(c) whether it is a fact that in the past
too, various such plans of commercialisation
have been shelved in view of the opposition
from various agencies;
(d) if so, whether Government have
explored to develop this piece of land into
a horticulture park or use for ballooning
carnivals, micro light tourist flights or as
National Air Museum; and
(e) if not, the reasons therefor?
Use of old 747 aircrafts
1906. PROF. SAIF-UD-DIN SOZ: Will
the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION be
pleased to state:
(a) whether he is aware that the age of
many 747 aircrafts is such that these can
no more be used as per International
standards; and
(b) whether any such aircrafts are still
in use and if so, the reasons therefor?
